opportunities.title: New research group by a dear former colleague now at the Institute of Astronomy, Bulgarian Academy of…
opportunities.content:
New research group by a dear former colleague now at the Institute of Astronomy, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences in Sofia: Cometary Life Cycle (CLIC) led by Rosita Kokotanekova ...

... is looking for two PhD students and two Postdocs to study the physical evolution of comet nuclei and their links to other small body populations (TNOs, Centaurs, irregular moons, and dormant comets). The project is also closely linked to Comet Interceptor and Rubin Observatory’s LSST. 

More at https://clic.kokotanekova.com/positions

Rosita adds: "I know Bulgaria is not a traditional top destination for young researchers, but this is a well-funded opportunity for independent, curious candidates open to the adventure." Deadlines to apply to go on this adventure are September 30 for the PhD students, and October 31 for the Postdocs.

opportunities.title: Wow, that's a lot of PhD and Postdoc positions opening up all at once (via…
opportunities.content:
Wow, that's a lot of PhD and Postdoc positions opening up all at once (via https://rss-parrot.net/u/bsky.app.profile.planetarynews.bsky.social/status/1781582682588180053):

A new Collaborative Research Center SFB 1759 on "Habitability as a fundamental planetary process: Towards a paradigm shift away from our perception of the uniqueness of Earth" funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) is being established at the Freie Universitat Berlin, Germany, starting October 1, 2026.

Within the SFB 1759, 18 Doctoral (75% E13 TV-L) and 6 Postdoctoral positions (100% E13 TV-L) are now open for application. Review of all applications will begin July 22, 2026 and will continue until all positions have been filled.

More information can be found on:

https://sfb1759-planetary-habitability.de/

@freieuniversitaet @dfg_public @planetary_research_jobs

opportunities.title: From Prof. Pavan Agrawal
opportunities.content:
From Prof. Pavan Agrawal:

"We are recruiting three PhD students for the 2026–27 Health Sciences intake at the Agrawal Lab, Centre for Molecular Neurosciences, KMC Manipal, MAHE."

"The lab studies how social experience and environmental stress reshape brain function and behavior using Drosophila genetics, functional genomics, behavioral neuroscience, and open-source tool development. Current projects span:

1. Cell-type specific molecular responses to social isolation
2. Wearable sensors, spatial behavior, and anxiety biology
3. Neuro-immune regulation of behavior under social stress

"Our work combines neurogenetics, transcriptomics, quantitative behavior, and machine-vision approaches, including DANCE, our open-source behavioral analysis platform recently published in eLife."
